timeline.event: Emperor Ashoka turns to Buddhism after the Kalinga War

timeline.event: Chandragupta I founds the Gupta Empire
timeline.label: c. 320 CE

timeline.label: 499 CE

timeline.event: The Delhi Sultanate is founded
Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut by sea from Portugal
Babur wins the First Battle of Panipat and founds the Mughal Empire
Akbar becomes Mughal emperor at the age of thirteen
The English East India Company receives its royal charter
Construction of the Taj Mahal begins
The East India Company wins the Battle of Plassey
The Indian Rebellion breaks out against Company rule
The Indian National Congress is founded
Rabindranath Tagore wins the Nobel Prize in Literature
Gandhi leads the Salt March to Dandi
India gains independence from British rule
India's constitution takes effect and it becomes a republic
India wins its first Cricket World Cup

places.name: New Delhi
places.clue: Laid out by architect Edwin Lutyens, it was inaugurated as British India's capital in 1931 and now seats India's government.

places.name: Taj Mahal
places.clue: Shah Jahan built this white marble mausoleum for his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in childbirth.

places.name: Mumbai
places.clue: Once seven separate islands, it was joined by land reclamation into one of the world's most populous cities.

places.name: Varanasi
places.clue: One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, its riverside ghats host the nightly Ganga Aarti ceremony.

places.name: Golden Temple, Amritsar
places.clue: Its community kitchen serves free vegetarian meals to tens of thousands of visitors every day, whatever their faith.

places.name: Hampi
places.clue: These boulder-strewn ruins were once Vijayanagara, capital of a mighty South Indian empire and among the largest cities of its age.

places.name: Kaziranga National Park
places.clue: This Brahmaputra floodplain shelters about two-thirds of the world's greater one-horned rhinos.

places.name: Meenakshi Temple, Madurai
places.clue: Its towering gateway gopurams are covered in thousands of brightly painted sculptures of gods, demons and animals.

places.name: Jaisalmer
places.clue: Nicknamed the Golden City, its sandstone fort is one of the few in the world where people still live inside the walls.

places.name: Dholavira
places.clue: This Harappan city in the salt flats of Kutch had clever reservoirs and a giant signboard written in Indus script.

places.name: Konark Sun Temple
places.clue: This 13th-century temple to the sun god is carved as a colossal stone chariot with 24 wheels, pulled by seven horses.

places.name: Mawsynram
places.clue: This village in the Khasi Hills is often called the wettest place on Earth, soaking up nearly 12 metres of rain a year.
